step: R7 claim-level prior-art attack vs US11896789B2 Shunt Flusher family

ceo_directive_compliance.directive: Map R7 limitations one-by-one against US11896789B2 / US20160038724A1. Separate literal anticipation / partial overlap / analogous teaching / genuinely missing. Do NOT say 'eShunt application is different, therefore novel.' The correct question: what claim limitation exists in R7 that the strongest prior-art combination does not teach, and why would that limitation matter?
ceo_directive_compliance.pushing_the_envelope: Different application is not automatically different invention. Discovery search finds candidates. Destruction search finds threats. Claim mapping determines whether the candidate survives. Only then does physics get expensive.

prior_art_patent.title: Shunt catheter flushing system
prior_art_patent.abstract: A device and system for flushing a shunt catheter utilizes the available CSF to flush a blocked catheter. The CSF is pressurized to a predetermined amount and then allowed to suddenly, rapidly and forcefully purge any occlusions. The rapid release of CSF produces flow jets from the catheter pores into the ventricle. This impulse, or 'cough', will push and divert choroid plexus and/or other blockages away from the pores.
prior_art_patent.claim_1_text: A system for flushing a shunt catheter, comprising: a catheter with a body having a lumen; a primary set of drain pores; a secondary set of drain pores with membranes configured to close the pores, the membranes ruptured upon application of fluid pressure to open the secondary set; and a pressure source configured to apply fluid pressure to rupture the membrane.
prior_art_patent.key_mechanism: Pressure source (reservoir) pressurizes CSF → membranes on secondary pores rupture → sudden CSF flush through secondary pores → 'cough' impulse clears obstruction from primary pores → debris pushed AWAY from catheter pores
prior_art_patent.autonomous_mode: Claim 11: 'membrane constructed to be ruptured upon application of fluid pressure to open secondary drain pores when the application of fluid pressure fails to unblock the primary set of drain pores' — this is an AUTOMATIC mode where obstruction triggers the flush

r7_proposed_limitations.L1: Endovascular eShunt (subarachnoid space → venous sinus drainage)
r7_proposed_limitations.L2: Pressure-activated mechanism (obstruction raises pressure → triggers clearing)
r7_proposed_limitations.L3: Distal debris transport (debris pushed toward venous system, not toward brain)
r7_proposed_limitations.L5: Valve architecture that opens wider under pressure
r7_proposed_limitations.L6: Restores CSF drainage without device removal or catheterization

L1_endovascular_eshunt.us11896789b2_teaching: VP shunt (ventricle→peritoneum). The patent is for a VENTRICULAR catheter with drain pores in the ventricle.
L1_endovascular_eshunt.overlap: PARTIAL — both are CSF shunts, but different drainage destinations (venous vs peritoneal)
L1_endovascular_eshunt.is_this_novel: WEAK — the drainage destination is a consequence of the eShunt's existing design, not a new invention. Applying a known flushing mechanism to an existing device (eShunt) is not a new mechanism invention.
L1_endovascular_eshunt.ceo_test: 'Different application is not automatically different invention.' The eShunt is a different application of the same flushing concept.

L2_pressure_activated.us11896789b2_teaching: Claim 11 explicitly teaches: 'membrane ruptured upon application of fluid pressure when application fails to unblock primary pores.' This is EXACTLY pressure-activated obstruction clearing.
L2_pressure_activated.overlap: LITERAL ANTICIPATION — the patent explicitly teaches pressure-activated clearing when obstruction occurs
L2_pressure_activated.is_this_novel: NO — the pressure-activation concept is directly anticipated by Claim 11

L3_distal_debris_transport.us11896789b2_teaching: The patent's 'cough' impulse pushes debris 'away from the pores' — in a VP shunt, this means debris is pushed into the VENTRICLE (proximal), not distally toward the peritoneum. The Shunt Flusher pushes debris PROXIMALLY (into the ventricle).
L3_distal_debris_transport.overlap: DIFFERENT — the Shunt Flusher pushes debris proximally (into ventricle); R7 pushes debris distally (toward venous system). This is a GENUINE difference.
L3_distal_debris_transport.is_this_novel: POTENTIALLY — the debris DIRECTION is different. But is this a claimable limitation? The Shunt Flusher's debris goes into the ventricle (where the choroid plexus is, causing the obstruction). R7's debris goes into the venous sinus (the drainage destination). This is a consequence of the device geometry, not a separate mechanism.
L3_distal_debris_transport.ceo_test: The debris direction difference is a consequence of the eShunt's existing drainage direction, not a new mechanism. R7 doesn't INVENT distal debris transport — it's what happens when you apply pressure-flush to an eShunt instead of a VP shunt.

L4_autonomous.us11896789b2_teaching: Claim 11: automatic mode where 'application of fluid pressure fails to unblock primary pores' triggers the secondary pore opening. This is AUTONOMOUS — obstruction triggers the flush without external actuation.
L4_autonomous.overlap: LITERAL ANTICIPATION — autonomous obstruction-triggered flushing is directly taught

L5_valve_architecture.us11896789b2_teaching: The patent uses RUPTURABLE MEMBRANES (not a valve that opens wider). The membranes are one-time-use — once ruptured, the secondary pores stay open permanently. This is DIFFERENT from a valve that opens and closes.
L5_valve_architecture.overlap: PARTIAL — both use pressure to open a flow path, but the mechanism differs (rupturable membrane vs reusable valve)
L5_valve_architecture.is_this_novel: POTENTIALLY — a reusable pressure-activated valve (vs one-time rupturable membrane) could be a different mechanism. But pressure-activated valves are well-known in shunt design (programmable valves, differential pressure valves). This is likely OBVIOUS over the combination of Shunt Flusher + known pressure valves.

L6_restores_without_removal.us11896789b2_teaching: The Shunt Flusher ALSO restores drainage without removal — the entire purpose is to flush obstruction in place.
L6_restores_without_removal.overlap: LITERAL ANTICIPATION — in-place clearing is the patent's core purpose

summary_of_mapping.assessment: R7's core mechanism (pressure-activated autonomous obstruction clearing) is LITERALLY ANTICIPATED by US11896789B2 Claim 11. The only genuinely different element is debris direction (distal/venous vs proximal/ventricular), but this is a CONSEQUENCE of the device geometry, not a new mechanism.

the_correct_question.ceo_test: What claim limitation exists in R7 that the strongest prior-art combination does not teach, and why would that limitation matter?
the_correct_question.answer: The only potentially novel limitation is L3: debris goes DISTALLY (toward venous system) instead of PROXIMALLY (toward ventricle). But this is not a MECHANISM difference — it's a CONSEQUENCE of applying the Shunt Flusher's pressure-clearing concept to an eShunt (which drains venously) instead of a VP shunt (which drains to peritoneum). The Shunt Flusher's debris goes into the ventricle because that's where the VP shunt's proximal pores are. R7's debris goes into the venous sinus because that's where the eShunt's distal end is. The debris direction is determined by the DEVICE GEOMETRY, not by a new mechanism.
the_correct_question.is_this_patentable: UNLIKELY — applying a known mechanism (pressure-activated flush, taught by US11896789B2) to a known device (eShunt) is likely OBVIOUS. The debris direction difference is inherent to the device, not an inventive step. A method claim ('method of clearing an eShunt obstruction by pressure-activated flush') might survive if the eShunt's specific geometry creates unexpected results (e.g., the venous drainage direction makes the flush safer than in VP shunts), but this would require evidence of unexpected results, not just 'different application.'

v14_adjudication.verdict: R7 FAILS — core mechanism literally anticipated by US11896789B2
rationale: 1. LITERAL ANTICIPATION: US11896789B2 Claim 11 explicitly teaches pressure-activated autonomous obstruction clearing. R7's L2 (pressure-activated), L4 (autonomous), and L6 (in-place clearing) are all directly anticipated.

2. DIFFERENT APPLICATION ≠ DIFFERENT INVENTION: Applying the Shunt Flusher concept to an eShunt is a different application, not a different invention. The CEO's principle applies: 'Different application is not automatically different invention.'

3. DEBRIS DIRECTION IS GEOMETRY, NOT MECHANISM: The only genuinely different element (L3: distal vs proximal debris) is a consequence of the eShunt's drainage geometry, not a new mechanism. The Shunt Flusher pushes debris toward the ventricle because VP shunt pores face the ventricle. R7 pushes debris toward the venous sinus because the eShunt drains venously. This is inherent to the device, not inventive.

4. VALVE VS MEMBRANE: R5 (reusable valve) vs Shunt Flusher (one-time rupturable membrane) is a minor engineering difference. Pressure-activated valves are well-known in shunt design. This is likely obvious over the combination.

5. NO UNEXPECTED RESULTS: R7 does not demonstrate that applying pressure-flush to an eShunt produces unexpected results (e.g., the venous drainage makes the flush unexpectedly safer). Without unexpected results, the application of a known method to a known device is obvious.
v14_adjudication.what_would_save_r7: R7 could survive if: (a) the eShunt's specific geometry creates an unexpected technical effect (e.g., the venous sinus pressure regime makes the flush work differently than in VP shunts), AND (b) this unexpected effect is demonstrated with evidence, not just hypothesized. But this would require engineering data, which we don't have yet.
v14_adjudication.r7_status: DEMOTED — fails claim-level prior-art attack. Core mechanism anticipated.

impact_on_remaining_candidates.r5_self_clearing_geometry: NOT AFFECTED by Shunt Flusher — R5 prevents obstruction through geometry, not pressure-flush. Different mechanism.
impact_on_remaining_candidates.r6_lumen_rerouting: NOT AFFECTED — R6 bypasses obstruction through secondary lumen, not pressure-flush. Different mechanism.
impact_on_remaining_candidates.r8_ultrasound: NOT AFFECTED — R8 uses external acoustic energy, not internal pressure. Different mechanism.
impact_on_remaining_candidates.r9_sacrificial_cartridge: NOT AFFECTED — R9 replaces the obstruction zone, not flushes it. Different mechanism.
impact_on_remaining_candidates.note: The Shunt Flusher specifically anticipates PRESSURE-ACTIVATED FLUSHING. It does not anticipate prevention (R5), bypass (R6), external energy (R8), or cartridge exchange (R9). These candidates remain viable.

next_step: R7 is demoted. The next candidate to attack from zero is R5 (self-clearing geometry) or R6 (lumen rerouting). Both are genuinely different mechanisms from pressure-flush. R5 prevents rather than treats; R6 bypasses rather than clears. Either could avoid the Shunt Flusher prior art entirely.
